report.verdict: Payouts and ledger services stand out, as does your ledger-recon project. I’d read to the end, but I’d still be guessing about what you did at Northwind Pay.
write_up: You’re a Senior Backend Engineer working on payouts and ledger services, with an open-source ledger project. It’s common to see a recent job described in one line, but here it leaves a recruiter guessing about your part in the work.

The best model is ledger-recon, near the bottom of your profile. It names the library, Go, 1,200 GitHub stars and use by three payment companies. That’s much more useful than the generic opening in your About.

Start with what you did at Northwind Pay, then bring the ledger project into your About and add your specialties to the headline. The earlier Kestrel Labs job is blank too. Together, those changes would give someone hiring for backend payments work a better picture of your work.

cards.cannot_tell: One line names the services but not your part in them. A recruiter can match payouts and ledger services, but has no words here for the specific work you did on either.

cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model: it names the library, the language and who uses it. Your job descriptions can name their work just as plainly.

fit.note: “Senior Backend Engineer” is in your headline and current title. “Payouts” and “ledger services” are in the Northwind Pay description. “Go” is in Top Skills and the ledger-recon project, while “ledger reconciliation” is in the project.
